questions.question: When a SQL query is translated into the algebra, what does each operator consume and return?
questions.anchor: produces again a relation as output
questions.expected_answer: Each operator takes a relation as input and produces a relation as output.

questions.question: Which operator keeps a relation's schema unchanged but returns only some of its tuples?
questions.anchor: unary operator that produces a new relation with the same schema
questions.expected_answer: Selection.

questions.question: Can you show a worked example of subtracting one relation from another?
questions.expected_answer: The difference example over the actor relations.

questions.question: Which join variant pairs tuples using an arbitrary boolean predicate instead of equality?
questions.expected_answer: The theta join.

questions.question: Which operator returns exactly those tuples of the left relation that find no match on the right?
questions.anchor: have no join partners in s
questions.expected_answer: The anti join.

questions.question: Which aggregate function yields the alphabetically first film title?
questions.expected_answer: MIN(Title).

questions.question: Which union variant applies when the two relations do not share a schema?
questions.anchor: schemas of r and s must be different
questions.expected_answer: The outer union.

questions.question: How is a query combining a length condition and a studio condition written as one algebra expression?
questions.expected_answer: Projection over the join of the two selections on Film.

questions.question: Why is a union cheaper to compute when duplicate tuples are permitted?
questions.expected_answer: Set semantics needs concatenation plus deduplication; multiset semantics needs only concatenation.

questions.question: Which elementary operations of a transaction actually touch the database?
questions.anchor: Elementary operations with respect to database
questions.expected_answer: read() and write().

questions.question: Which component orders concurrent operations and enforces the consistency guarantees?
questions.anchor: Order of the operations in an execution plan
questions.expected_answer: The transaction manager.

questions.question: What anomaly occurs when reading the same value twice in one transaction returns different results?
questions.anchor: Read of A again provides another
questions.expected_answer: A nonrepeatable read.

questions.question: Which isolation level permits reading data that has not been committed yet?
questions.anchor: Access to not fixed data possible
questions.expected_answer: read uncommitted.

questions.question: When can an interleaved execution be treated as equivalent to running the transactions one after another?
questions.anchor: conflict equivalent to a serial schedule
questions.expected_answer: When it is conflict equivalent to a serial schedule.

questions.question: Which property of the conflict graph proves serialisability, and how is that proof structured?
questions.anchor: Induction over the number of transactions
questions.expected_answer: A cycle-free conflict graph, proved by induction over the number of transactions.

questions.question: Can you show an example where two transactions lock and release the same objects in turn?
questions.expected_answer: The T1/T3 trace with l(A), write, u(A) on A and B.

questions.question: How is the basic SELECT-FROM-WHERE form expressed in the grammar used for parsing?
questions.expected_answer: <SFW> ::= SELECT <SelList> FROM <FromList> WHERE <Condition>

questions.question: What is produced from a parse tree in the stage before physical planning?
questions.expected_answer: An optimal logical query plan.

questions.question: What has to stay unchanged when a query plan is rewritten for efficiency?
questions.expected_answer: The semantics of the query.

questions.question: Which selection rewriting rule stops being valid once duplicates are allowed?
questions.expected_answer: The disjunction rule rewriting a selection into a union.

questions.question: Which rewriting turns a cross product followed by a filter into a single operator?
questions.expected_answer: Combining selections with cross products to form joins.

questions.question: How can you inspect the plan a database chose for a query?
questions.expected_answer: Through the optimiser's explain() function.

questions.question: What does proving NP-hardness establish about a problem?
questions.anchor: Proof of the NP-hardness is a
questions.expected_answer: It is a sufficient criterion for characterising the problem's difficulty.

questions.question: In what units can the optimiser express its cost estimates?
questions.expected_answer: Abstract units such as I/O operations, energy in kWh or cloud cost.

questions.question: Which quantity estimates how many tuples survive an operator relative to its input?
questions.anchor: estimates the number of the qualifying
questions.expected_answer: The selectivity (sf).

questions.question: How large was the market cited in the motivation, and how fast was it growing?
questions.expected_answer: $122 billion in 2016, growing 11.3% per year.

questions.question: Where can a ranking of database management systems be looked up?
questions.expected_answer: At db-engines.com/en/ranking.

questions.question: Which scenario illustrates how data was handled before database systems existed?
questions.anchor: Three client advisors Alfred, Beate, and Carlo
questions.expected_answer: Data processing in an insurance company with three client advisors.

questions.question: What caveat is given about the data-volume figures shown?
questions.expected_answer: They are outdated; actual volumes are much larger now.

questions.question: What goes wrong when several programs work on the same files at once without a database?
questions.anchor: cannot work on the same data in parallel without interfering
questions.expected_answer: They interfere with one another.

questions.question: Which mechanisms does a database provide to keep stored data valid?
questions.expected_answer: Data types, keys and UNIQUE, foreign keys, and access rights.

questions.question: In which direction is a query plan evaluated?
questions.anchor: Execution from the sources to the root
questions.expected_answer: From the sources at the leaves up to the root.

questions.question: Which tables make up the example order schema used to introduce distributed data?
questions.expected_answer: Orders, Order, Bookgroup, Book, Customer, Day, Month and Year.

questions.question: Which metric characterises the performance of an operational transaction workload?
questions.expected_answer: Transactions per second.

questions.question: How does a federated system differ from copying data into a separate analytical store?
questions.anchor: analytical views that fetch the data on demand
questions.expected_answer: A federated system fetches on demand through analytical views; the alternative copies data across periodically.

questions.question: Which regulation-driven request motivates integrating data held across separate shop systems?
questions.expected_answer: A GDPR/DSGVO subject access request.

questions.question: Which application of data integration is illustrated by searching across web tables?
questions.expected_answer: Information retrieval over web tables.

questions.question: Which two broad categories of obstacle make combining data sources hard?
questions.expected_answer: System-level reasons and logical reasons.

questions.question: What distinguishes the warehouse-style pipeline from the lake-style one?
questions.anchor: copied from disparate sources into a joint representation
questions.expected_answer: ETL transforms while copying (warehouse); ELT loads first and transforms later (lake).

questions.question: Which publication is cited as the reference for federated database systems?
questions.expected_answer: Sheth and Larson, on managing distributed, heterogeneous and autonomous databases.

questions.question: Which topics do the four practical assignments cover?
questions.expected_answer: Similarity measures, data profiling, data matching and duplicate detection.

questions.question: What makes a set of attributes usable as a key?
questions.anchor: the same values in all key attributes
questions.expected_answer: No two entities of the type share values across all key attributes.

questions.question: Which statements can violate a key constraint, and which cannot?
questions.expected_answer: INSERT and UPDATE can; DELETE cannot.

questions.question: Can you show a table definition declaring both a composite primary key and a foreign key?
questions.expected_answer: The Employee table example.

questions.question: Besides rejecting or cascading, what third response to a foreign-key violation is available?
questions.anchor: try to solve violation with null
questions.expected_answer: Setting the referencing value to null, rejecting otherwise.

questions.question: How can constraint checking be postponed until the end of a transaction, and what is the default?
questions.anchor: Check the constraint for each update of the database
questions.expected_answer: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; the default is NOT DEFERRABLE.

questions.question: Which clause expresses an arbitrary condition on a single column's values?
questions.expected_answer: An attribute-based CHECK constraint.

questions.question: Why should a constraint be given an explicit name when it is created?
questions.expected_answer: Because it can only be altered later by name; otherwise the DBMS assigns a cryptic internal one.

questions.question: What is the trade-off between a database-wide boolean condition and an event-driven action?
questions.expected_answer: Assertions are simple for admins but hard to implement efficiently; triggers are event-driven and harder to author.

questions.question: How do attribute-based and tuple-based checks differ in when they are evaluated?
questions.expected_answer: Attribute-based checks fire on insert or update of that attribute; tuple-based checks on the whole relation.
